schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE alignment
(
    id        INTEGER not null
            primary key,
    alignment TEXT default NULL
);

CREATE TABLE attribute
(
    id             INTEGER not null
            primary key,
    attribute_name TEXT default NULL
);

CREATE TABLE colour
(
    id     INTEGER not null
            primary key,
    colour TEXT default NULL
);

CREATE TABLE gender
(
    id     INTEGER not null
            primary key,
    gender TEXT default NULL
);

CREATE TABLE publisher
(
    id             INTEGER not null
            primary key,
    publisher_name TEXT default NULL
);

CREATE TABLE race
(
    id   INTEGER not null
            primary key,
    race TEXT default NULL
);

CREATE TABLE superhero
(
    id             INTEGER not null
            primary key,
    superhero_name TEXT default NULL,
    full_name      TEXT default NULL,
    gender_id      INTEGER          default NULL,
    eye_colour_id  INTEGER          default NULL,
    hair_colour_id INTEGER          default NULL,
    skin_colour_id INTEGER          default NULL,
    race_id        INTEGER          default NULL,
    publisher_id   INTEGER          default NULL,
    alignment_id   INTEGER          default NULL,
    height_cm      INTEGER          default NULL,
    weight_kg      INTEGER          default NULL,
    foreign key (alignment_id) references alignment(id),
    foreign key (eye_colour_id) references colour(id),
    foreign key (gender_id) references gender(id),
    foreign key (hair_colour_id) references colour(id),
    foreign key (publisher_id) references publisher(id),
    foreign key (race_id) references race(id),
    foreign key (skin_colour_id) references colour(id)
);

CREATE TABLE hero_attribute
(
    hero_id         INTEGER default NULL,
    attribute_id    INTEGER default NULL,
    attribute_value INTEGER default NULL,
    foreign key (attribute_id) references attribute(id),
    foreign key (hero_id) references superhero(id)
);

CREATE TABLE superpower
(
    id         INTEGER not null
            primary key,
    power_name TEXT default NULL
);

CREATE TABLE hero_power
(
    hero_id  INTEGER default NULL,
    power_id INTEGER default NULL,
    foreign key (hero_id) references superhero(id),
    foreign key (power_id) references superpower(id)
);
q1: SELECT T3.race FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.hero_id INNER JOIN race AS T3 ON T1.race_id = T3.id ORDER BY T2.attribute_value DESC LIMIT 1
q2: SELECT T3.race FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.hero_id INNER JOIN race AS T3 ON T1.race_id = T3.id WHERE T2.attribute_value = (SELECT MAX(attribute_value) FROM hero_attribute)

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT T3.race FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.hero_id INNER JOIN race AS T3 ON T1.race_id = T3.id WHERE T2.attribute_value = (SELECT MAX(attribute_value) FROM hero_attribute)
counterexample: INSERT INTO publisher (id, publisher_name) VALUES (1, 'Publisher A'); INSERT INTO race (id, race) VALUES (1, 'Race A'), (2, 'Race B'); INSERT INTO superhero (id, publisher_id, race_id) VALUES (1, 1, 1), (2, 1, 2); INSERT INTO hero_attribute (hero_id, attribute_value) VALUES (1, 100), (2, 100);
explanation: Q1 orders the superheroes by the highest attribute value and then selects the race of the first one, while Q2 filters the superheroes by the highest attribute value and then selects the race of all of them. Therefore, Q1 and Q2 can return different results if there are multiple superheroes with the same highest attribute value.
counterexample_dsp: Create two superheroes with the same highest attribute value, but different races. Q1 will return the race of the first superhero, while Q2 will return the race of both superheroes.
